query: What is the speed of light?
generated_response: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately \(299,792,458\) meters per second (m/s). This constant is known as the speed of light and was first measured by Albert Einstein in 1905 using the Michelson-Morley experiment. The speed of light is fundamental to our understanding of the universe and plays a crucial role in many aspects of physics, including relativity and electromagnetism.
